ops.title: Papercut #14 misdiagnosed: localdir sources skipped manifest drilling, not kind resolution
ops.body:
Papercut #14 (`2fe6f03` index 14, 2026-07-26) is **fixed**, but its diagnosis and its
prescribed remedy were both wrong. Recording the correction so nobody implements the
remedy it asked for.

## What the papercut claimed

> a localdir source doesn't serve the json/sh-kind shared fragments the way the
> `github:` source does […] Making localdir sources resolve non-md fragment kinds
> would close it.

## Why that is wrong

`Resolver.Resolve` in cc-guides `source/resolver.go` is **kind-agnostic and
source-agnostic**. It builds `filepath.Join(src.dir, kind.String(), name+kind.Ext())`
and calls `os.ReadFile`. There is no per-kind gate anywhere on the resolve path, and
no branch that distinguishes a localdir source from a `github:` one once the source
dir is known. "Make localdir sources resolve non-md kinds" describes removing a gate
that does not exist.

## The actual cause

The localdir branch of `Resolver.source` set `dir = spec` **verbatim**, skipping the
manifest drilling the `github:` branch performs via `manifestGuidesDir`. Pointed at a
pack root, it therefore looked for fragments directly under the checkout root instead
of under the manifest's `guides` dir (`plugin/guides/` for cc-skills). Nothing was
found under **any** kind.

The error message said so the whole time: the abort was `ErrUnknownFragment`
("unknown fragment"), not `ErrKindMismatch`. A genuine kind-serving gap would have
produced the latter. `settings-base` merely happened to be the first artifact
rendered, which made an unconditional failure look kind-specific.

## The fix

cc-guides `f746108` — a local dir carrying a `cc-guides.toml` now drills through its
manifest exactly as a manifest-form `github:` spec does, via a new `localGuidesDir`
reusing the existing `manifestGuidesDir` (retargeted from a `Spec` to a label string).
A dir with no manifest stays the guides dir itself, which every existing fixture
relies on. A malformed manifest or a missing `guides` dir is a hard error, matching
the `github:` path — silently falling back would resurface a typo'd `guides` path as
a bare "unknown fragment", which is the exact confusion this papercut records.

Verified end to end in a cc-context scratch tree: the installed cask binary aborts
with `unknown fragment: cc-skills:settings-base (kind json)`; a local build renders
all 8 artifacts including `settings.json` and `AGENTS.md`.

## Carry-forward

The papercut's *symptom* report was accurate and the fail-safe behavior it noted
(nothing written on abort) held. Only the mechanism and remedy were wrong — inferred
from the symptom rather than read out of the resolver. Read the error's sentinel type
before theorizing about the cause; `ErrUnknownFragment` vs `ErrKindMismatch` would
have pointed at the right branch immediately.

Note: `--source alias=<localdir>` still requires a full, non-path-scoped render.
That refusal (`internal/cli/render.go` `scopedPins`, `internal/cli/check.go`) is a
deliberate pin-consistency invariant, not part of this bug, and was left alone.
